text:
cs-jordan: Hey team — BrightCart just escalated. During their hourly traffic burst we saw ~30s tail latencies and a rash of 429s. They report the dedicated pool didn’t scale up for ~8 minutes. They attached traces and say they saw attach failures and auth errors in our logs.
ops-alert-bot: Alert: DedicatedAutoscalerDelay BrightCart tenant_id=brightcart svc=dedicated-autoscaler severity=high
devon: Acknowledged. Any repro steps or minimal timelines?
cs-jordan: Spike timeline: 13:02 -> 13:06 UTC traffic jumped from ~1k RPS -> ~5k RPS. Warm pool had min_replicas=2, max=50, burst enabled. Controller logs show repeated attach_denied + probe timeout.
maria: Quick grab from controller logs:```
WARN  attach_controller.go:142 attach failed: token refresh failed for tenant brightcart: 401 unauthorized
ERROR autoscaler.go:311 warmpool attach backoff count=6 last_err="registry pull 503"
ERROR probe.go:78 probe timeout after 10s waiting for ready
```
nikhil: Two suspects: (1) token rotation / service-account key rotation - agents couldn't attach because auth failed, (2) registry/imagepull latencies causing warm pods to remain unready so autoscaler saw fewer ready replicas and didn't meet its smoothing thresholds.
devon: Good call. Can you dump recent token rotation events and registry latency during spike? Also confirm if min_replicas floor blocked horizontal scale due to step-size heuristic.
maria: Registry metrics show a short 90s window of elevated 503s from our upstream registry region starting 13:01:45. Service account key rotation job for BrightCart ran at 12:59:50 and reported success, but the agent logs show the new key never propagated to some attach workers until 13:05:xx.
cs-jordan: Customer says they saw imagepull errors in container events too. They pasted these:```
Back-off pulling image "gcr.io/brightcart/model:v1.2"
Failed to pull image "gcr.io/brightcart/model:v1.2": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to fetch token: 401
```
devon: Repro plan (short): 1) reproduce token rotation hang locally 2) reproduce registry 503 under load 3) run a controlled spike to observe autoscaler smoothing behavior. Commands I'll try:```
# simulate load
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s https://dedicated-api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <brightcart-token>"
# rotate sa key (dev env)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/key.json --iam-account=brightcart-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
kubectl -n tenants patch secret brightcart-sa-secret --from-file=key.json
```
nikhil: Temporary mitigations for customer: 1) bump min_replicas to 10 for the next 30m so warmpool has headroom, 2) enable reserved burst allocation while registry heals, 3) set fallback route to hosted-model for 2-5m to avoid 429s.
linda: Executed (1) and (2) for BrightCart. Increased min_replicas -> 10 and flipped burst policy. Customer reports latencies dropped and 429s mostly stopped after ~3 minutes. :thumbsup:
cs-jordan: Customer accepted mitigations but wants RCA and permanent fix. They said this is causing churn with their ops team.
maria: I'll correlate registry region metrics and our agent propagation window. Early hypothesis: our token rotation controller marked keys rotated but a subset of attach workers read from an eventual-consistency cache and used stale tokens for ~4m. That combined with registry failures created a two-hit failure.
devon: I'll open a follow-up ticket linking logs and the repro commands, and schedule a short postmortem with eng-runtime and registry teams. @nikhil can you check autoscaler smoothing thresholds? We may need a fast-path when warmpool attach failures exceed X in Ys to bypass step-hysteresis.
nikhil: Yep. I'll instrument a metric for consecutive attach backoffs and add an emergency-fastscale route if threshold exceeded.
cs-jordan: Thanks all — keeping BrightCart updated. I'll paste customer logs into the ticket and mark P1 until we have root cause.
ops-alert-bot: Incident created: INC-5370001 assigned=eng-runtime severity=high link=https://incidents.redwood/INC-5370001
